name_reason: Already compliant: data_fd2_battle_ prefix (game battle-core global), descriptor accurately reflects purpose (per-glyph target runtime_char index queue for the floating damage-number / MISS overlay) and data type (queue/array). No Ghidra address residue; '200' is not baked into the name. Verified against accessors fd2_show_damage_number (write @0x1e19e), fd2_show_miss_indicator (write @0x1e24e), fd2_animate_spell_projectile_paths (read @0x1e01d).
purpose: Runtime scratch queue of per-glyph target runtime_char indices for the floating damage-number / MISS overlay rendered above a target's head during a battle spell/attack.
logic_summary: Third (last) of three contiguous 200-byte parallel SoA queues (sprite_id @0x53c6c, x_offset @0x53d34, target_char_idx @0x53dfc) sharing one running write index data_fd2_battle_spell_aoe_count_and_fx_queue_idx @0x53ec4 (advanced by 4 per enqueue). Producers fd2_show_damage_number and fd2_show_miss_indicator append 4 entries per call, each storing (byte)target_char_idx. Consumer fd2_animate_spell_projectile_paths walks slots 0..count-1 and uses each value as an index into runtime_char_array to fetch the target's bPos_x/bPos_y board position when placing the glyph in the framebuffer. 200-byte extent fixed by the 0xC8 gap from 0x53dfc to 0x53ec4.
element_semantics: Each element is a runtime_char_array index (target character index) for one enqueued overlay glyph; 8-bit MOV stores in producers and byte-index use in consumer prove unsigned 1-byte element with stride 1.
comment_original_issue: src comment cited the wrong instruction address for fd2_show_damage_number's target_char_idx store: it listed @0x1E1C7 (which is actually the sibling sprite_id store) instead of the actual store @0x1E19E (MOV byte ptr [EBX+EAX*1+0x53DFC],DL). The rest of the comment block was accurate.
notes: src comment block (btltab2.c lines ~305-333) corrected: fd2_show_damage_number store address fixed 0x1E1C7 -> 0x1E19E and its store instruction added for symmetry with the sibling. Ghidra side: the existing data documentation lived in the deprecated PRE_COMMENT (PLATE_COMMENT was null); migrated the (already-accurate) content into PLATE_COMMENT via run_script_inline Java API per project_ghidra_data_plate_mechanism, and cleared PRE_COMMENT to avoid duplication. No game logic / type / declaration changed. Datatype already uint8/byte[200] in both src and Ghidra (confirmed DT=byte[200] LEN=200). is_const=false because game code writes the array (producers WRITE).
